Strait of Hormuz Status: October 13, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  227 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
13 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.88 -0.57 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 The Financial Times and Anadolu Ajansı report ships in the Strait of Hormuz were hit in the worst spate of attacks since the war began, with six vessels targeted in a single day.

02 Anadolu Ajansı and WANA News Agency report a tanker caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; Iranian state media, relayed by Anadolu Ajansı and WANA, claim the vessel switched off its tracking and attempted an unauthorized crossing.

03 Brent stood at $105.88, down 0.57% over 24 hours, as of 18:15 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz is sustaining its heaviest single-day attack tempo since the war began, with the Financial Times and Anadolu Ajansı both reporting that six vessels were struck in one day, the highest toll since hostilities started. Gulf News and marketscreener.com report that three vessels were struck by unknown projectiles, with UKMTO cited as the source; separately, Yeni Şafak English reports the IRGC struck a third tanker in the strait. Iranian state media, also carried by Anadolu Ajansı and WANA News Agency, claim an oil tanker that disabled its tracking systems and attempted an unauthorized crossing caught fire and sustained damage in the eastern strait; Tehran characterizes the vessel as non-compliant. A Newsquawk item, flagged as unverified and single-source, quotes a US official via Al Jazeera describing Iran's maritime attacks as unjustified acts of aggression that Washington is closely monitoring. On the crew-casualty front, the case of two missing Indian seafarers from a drone strike on a vessel, reported on October 11, remains in the feed with no new update in this window. Throughput remains deeply suppressed: IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $105.88, down 0.57% over 24 hours, as of 18:15 UTC. Iran's foreign ministry, per background reporting, says Tehran is still reviewing Washington's reply to its seven conditions and will respond through intermediaries. As of 18:22 UTC, 144 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
